text: His first name was Vithal. The third of five brothers, he was a self-taught pleader who practiced for a time in Godhra. His younger brother was also a pleader, and both men dreamed of going to England to become a barrister. The younger brother saved money and obtained documents to realize his dream; however Vithal convinced him that he as the elder brother should go instead. After returning to India as a barrister, Vithal got interested in politics and eventually co-founded the Swaraj Party. He went on to become the first Indian speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly, the legislative body of the British Raj. Despite these accomplishments, his position in history is dwarfed by that of his younger brother. Name his younger brother.
